theses.name: Lexinfintech Holdings Ltd. Class A
theses.one_liner: Lexin is guiding to a 3Q26 net loss and 华泰 now models a FY2026 loss of RMB 500m with 90-day+ delinquency at 3.6% and provision coverage down to 230% - at 0.07x book.
theses.thesis: The bull case is a deep-value floor: a USD 0.72 close, 0.90x TTM earnings, 0.072x book, TTM free cash flow of RMB 3.16bn (USD 445.6m) on a USD 126.7m market cap - a 352% FCF yield - and the X crowd is explicitly long exactly that, trading the basket as 'priced for bankruptcy'. The mechanism against it is a credit cycle that is still forming rather than finished: 2Q26 net profit of RMB 101m fell 80% YoY and about 50% QoQ, 90-day+ delinquency rose to 3.6% (from 3.5% in 1Q26 and 3.1% in 4Q25), provision coverage fell to 230%, loan volume was RMB 55.4bn (-4.3% QoQ; under RMB 35bn excluding the tech-services business) and management guided to a 3Q26 net loss. 华泰证券's 2 Sep 2026 note forecasts a full-year 2026 net loss of RMB 500m against RMB 1.7bn of FY2025 profit and expects 3Q26 lending to contract sharply. The screen itself does not underwrite the short - LX carries the lowest thesis and conviction scores in this batch (34.6 and 32.0) and a 0.0/100 valuation component - so this is a falling-credit-cycle trade against a value bid, not a valuation short.
bear_points: 2Q26 net profit of RMB 101m was -80% YoY and -49.7% QoQ, with management guiding to a 3Q26 net loss (Q2 2026 earnings call, 31 Aug 2026; 华泰证券, 2 Sep 2026).

Asset quality is still deteriorating while coverage falls: 90-day+ delinquency 3.6% (1Q26 3.5%, 4Q25 3.1%) and provision coverage cut to 230% (华泰证券, 2 Sep 2026); 1Q26 credit cost was already 5.28% and marketing cost 2.12% (华泰证券, 26 May 2026).

Volume is shrinking at the core: 2Q26 lending of RMB 55.4bn (-4.3% QoQ) and under RMB 35bn excluding the tech-services business, with 华泰 expecting a sharp 3Q26 contraction on industry funding tightness and modelling a FY2026 net loss of RMB 500m.

Quarterly net margin has fallen for four straight quarters - 15.2% (3Q25) to 7.0% (4Q25) to 6.0% (1Q26) to 3.15% (2Q26) - while the shareholder-return props were pulled: the dividend moves from semi-annual to annual (Q2 2026 call) and Citi says the buyback is paused pending regulatory clarity (25 May 2026).

No published target is near spot: the newest in the bundle are 华泰证券 at USD 2.9 (26 May 2026, with the 2 Sep 2026 note moving to a loss forecast) and Citi at USD 4.38 (25 May 2026) against a USD 0.72 close, and SI is only 1.26% (4,616,015 shares) - nobody is positioned for the deterioration.
risks_to_short: The valuation floor is the whole problem: 0.072x book, 0.90x TTM earnings and a 352% TTM FCF yield (RMB 3.16bn of free cash flow on a USD 126.7m market cap), with the screen's valuation component at 0.0/100. The equity is already priced for a severe credit cycle, so the short needs further deterioration, not merely bad news.

The public holders are explicitly on the other side of this trade: @westlakecap (21 Sep 2026) is long $LX at '0.07x book' and calls the basket '$LU $QFIN $FINV $XYF $YRD $LX priced for bankruptcy, not a smaller industry that still operates', while @hardmoney_jack (18 Sep 2026) notes '$LX has more EPS than the current stock price' - a live value bid, not an abandoned stock.

Peers show Lexin losing share more slowly than the industry: UBS (19 Mar 2026) recorded Q4 volume -2% QoQ at LX versus -22% at QFIN and -19% at FINV, with API-channel loans rising to 20% of volume; relative share gain inside a shrinking industry is the re-rate mechanic, and with SI at 1.26% and a 90/100 borrow score there is no crowded short to squeeze.

Company-controlled remedies and carry both work against the position: a cancellation of 20m ADS equal to about 12% of share capital was flagged in the 1Q26 call (25 May 2026) alongside a paused buyback that Citi expects to be revisited by end-2026, and the 4Q25 dividend of USD 0.188 per ADS was a 7.3% yield with UBS valuing the stock at a 12.4% dividend yield (13 Jan 2026) - so even a reduced annual payout is a carry cost.
catalysts: 3Q26 results, which management has already guided to a net loss (Q2 2026 call, 31 Aug 2026).
Whether FY2026 lands at 华泰证券's RMB 500m loss forecast (2 Sep 2026) against RMB 1.7bn of FY2025 profit.

theses.name: ATA Creativity Global
theses.one_liner: ATA Creativity's operating loss widened to -24.6% of revenue and FY2025 missed its own guidance, but USD 4.6m of book equity and USD 0.5m turnover make the short unworkable.
theses.thesis: The bear mechanism is a stalled education business with no asset floor. FY2025 revenue was USD 37.4m, essentially flat on FY2024 (+0.1%) and -10.5% below the prior TTM, with the operating margin widening to -24.6% from -15.8% in FY2024 and -18.7% in FY2023, TTM free cash flow of -USD 2.4m, and a Q4 2025 net margin of -29.5%. At 11.9x book the entire equity backing is about USD 4.6m, and EV of +USD 44.9m against a USD 54.8m market cap confirms there is no cash cushion - so a loss-making year eats a meaningful share of the book. What makes this a paper short is scale and evidence: ADT of USD 500.7k, no float data, an unknown borrow (the short interest ratio prints exactly 1.0), and 12 AlphaEngine documents that are all the company's own call transcripts with no rating, target or estimate anywhere.
bear_points: Revenue stopped growing: FY2025 revenue USD 37.4m was essentially flat against FY2024's USD 37.2m after +19.1% in FY2024, and TTM revenue is -10.5% YoY with student enrolment down 19.4% YoY in Q1 2025.

Guidance was missed: the company repeated a FY2025 revenue guide of RMB 276-281m on its Q2 and Q3 2025 calls, and the Q4 2025 call reports FY2025 revenue of RMB 268.1m - below the low end of the range.
Cost cuts are not holding the operating line: operating margin -24.6% in FY2025 versus -15.8% in FY2024 and -18.7% in FY2023, with a Q4 2025 net margin of -29.5% and TTM net margin of -17.9%.

There is no asset floor: 11.94x book means book equity of about USD 4.6m behind a USD 54.8m market cap, and EV of +USD 44.9m confirms the company is not net cash, so the equity is a thin residual on a loss-making business rather than a cash-backed stub.

Cash generation is negative and small in absolute terms: TTM operating cash flow -USD 2.2m and free cash flow -USD 2.4m (FCF yield -4.4%), against a USD 4.6m book - one more loss year is a material fraction of the equity.
risks_to_short: The company has been printing profitable quarters: net margin was +13.1% in Q4 2024 and +3.5% in Q3 2025, and the Q3 2025 call had operating expenses down 22.4% with the operating loss narrowed to RMB 10.6m - the cost programme can plausibly turn the operating line positive.

No mechanical net-cash blocker, but a hard liquidity one: EV is positive at USD 44.9m, so the balance sheet is not the obstacle; ADT of USD 500.7k, no float data and a 0.439 tradability gate (liquidity component 18.6/100) are.

Borrow is unknown rather than confirmed: the short interest ratio prints exactly 1.0 with no float data, which the screen flags as 'SI at floor/unknown' and scores as unknown (50/100), so a short can be right on the business and still unable to establish or hold the position.

An 11.9x book multiple on USD 4.6m of equity is also a squeeze setup: any equity raise at a premium, strategic investment, or a single profitable year re-rates a stock this thin, and with 13,035 shares short the float is effectively unmeasured.
catalysts: FY2026 revenue guidance and whether the 2026 cost-reduction plan described on the Q4 2025 call lifts operating margin above zero.
Enrolment in portfolio training, which was 71.9% of Q3 2025 revenue.
Quarterly operating cash flow, -USD 2.2m on a TTM basis against a book of about USD 4.6m.
Any equity issuance or strategic investment, given how thin the equity base is.
The next quarterly call: the last two prints (Q4 2025 at -29.5% net margin, Q3 2025 at +3.5%) diverged sharply.

theses.name: Hello Group Inc.
theses.one_liner: Hello Group trades below net cash with a 19% FCF yield, but domestic revenue fell 16.7% in 2Q26 and the special dividend was cut to USD 0.30 from 0.54 - a value trap, not a short.
theses.thesis: Hello Group is the cleanest structural-decay story in the batch and is simultaneously unhookable. 2Q26 revenue was RMB 2.486bn, -5.1% YoY, with domestic revenue down 16.7% to RMB 1.813bn, and management guided 3Q26 to RMB 2.4-2.5bn, or -5.7% to -9.4%, below consensus (Huatai, 2026-09-07; CICC, 2026-09-04). The only growth is overseas, +52% YoY to 27.1% of revenue, at a lower margin mix. The mechanism is that the cash return underpinning the valuation is being cut - the FY2025 special dividend fell to USD 0.30 per ADS from USD 0.54 and Morgan Stanley's final action before discontinuing coverage was Underweight with a 5.70 target. But EV is -USD 37.5m against a USD 722.5m market cap, so the equity already trades below net cash; this is a documented value trap and should not be sized as a short.
bear_points: Revenue is shrinking with a worse guide: 2Q26 total revenue RMB 2.486bn, -5.1% YoY, with domestic revenue -16.7% to RMB 1.813bn, and 3Q26 guided to RMB 2.4-2.5bn, -5.7% to -9.4% (Huatai, 2026-09-07; CICC, 2026-09-04).

The growth engine is margin-dilutive and was marked down: overseas revenue RMB 673m, +52% YoY and 27.1% of total, but the FY26 overseas target was cut to RMB 2.8-2.9bn from RMB 3.0bn (CICC transcript, 2026-09-03).
The user base is thinning: Tantan paying users fell to 500k from 600k in 1Q26, and Momo VAS revenue was RMB 1.54bn, -16% YoY (CICC, 2026-09-03).
Capital return was cut: the FY2025 special dividend fell to USD 0.30 per ADS from USD 0.54 (Morgan Stanley, 2026-03-16).

Screen decay supports it: a -8.1% three-year revenue CAGR and FY2025 revenue of RMB 10.09bn versus RMB 13.02bn in FY2022.
risks_to_short: Trades below net cash: EV is -USD 37.5m against a USD 722.5m market cap (screen); Huatai (2026-03-20) put year-end net cash at RMB 8.67bn, above the market cap, and Morgan Stanley's final SOTP used 5x 2026E earnings with net cash at a 20% discount.

Cash generation and buyback: TTM free cash flow USD 138.6m for a 19.2% FCF yield, with a remaining buyback authorization of USD 107.2m (about 12% of market cap) plus a USD 42.6m special dividend (UBS, 2026-03-18).
The print itself turned: 2Q26 non-GAAP net profit was RMB 274m, a swing from a RMB 96m loss a year earlier, with overseas operating profit positive and Yaahlan at break-even (CICC, 2026-09-03/04).

The Street is split rather than bearish: Huatai Buy PT 6.71 (2026-09-07), Deutsche Bank Buy PT 9.2 and UBS Buy PT 9 (both 2026-06-03) against a 4.93 close, i.e. targets 36-87% above the price. theses.name: Sohu.com Limited
theses.one_liner: Sohu's 1.5x P/E is one-off: a USD 285m Changyou tax reversal flatters TTM earnings while the operating business loses money and free cash flow is negative.
theses.thesis: The screen shows a 1.5x P/E and 0.27x book, which reads as a deep-value short. The actual business is a shrinking portal plus Changyou, and the TTM profit is an accounting event: FY2025 profit includes a USD 285m Changyou income-tax reversal, while the FY2025 operating margin was -16.0% and TTM operating cash flow was -USD 4.8m. Revenue has compounded at -7.2% over three years, Q2 2026 non-GAAP net income was only about USD 0.5m on USD 136m of revenue, and Citi's read on 3Q26 guidance was mixed (advertising above, games below). The mechanism is optical-valuation deflation rather than a solvency event, which is exactly why the screen's weakness component is only 13.1/100 and the name scores 26.2/100 on shortability.
bear_points: TTM net income of USD 229.6m is not earning power: FY2025 profit includes a USD 285m Changyou income-tax reversal (Q4 2025 earnings call), and the FY2025 operating margin was -16.0% with FY2024 at -18.3%.

The business does not generate cash: TTM operating cash flow -USD 4.8m and TTM free cash flow -USD 5.4m, with the screen flagging 'cash burner'; revenue has fallen from USD 733m (2022) to USD 600.8m TTM, a -7.2% three-year CAGR.
Q2 2026 was essentially break-even below the revenue line: revenue USD 136m (+7% YoY) but GAAP net income of USD 20k (earnings call) and non-GAAP net income of about USD 0.5m (Citi, 2026-08-10).

The profit base is one legacy game IP: Citi's 3Q25 note attributed the beat to TLBB Return, after which management guided 4Q25 games revenue down 24-30% QoQ and a return to a USD 25-35m adjusted loss.
Advertising, the second leg, is small and was guided down: 1Q26 marketing revenue was USD 13m, -8% YoY (earnings call), after Citi's 4Q25 note flagged 1Q26 ad revenue guided -20% to -27% YoY.
risks_to_short: Net cash is about USD 128m, roughly 37% of the USD 345m market cap (EV USD 216.8m versus market cap USD 345.2m), and of the USD 150m buyback authorisation USD 124m is already done; the Q2 2026 call converted the programme to open-ended, which is a standing bid under the stock.

Citi has stayed at Buy through every print and holds a USD 20 target (cut from USD 22 on 2026-05-22) against a USD 13.11 close - roughly 50% of published upside from the only live analyst covering the name.

Games can surprise positively against low guidance: TLBB Return delivered a USD 9m adjusted profit in 3Q25 versus guidance for a USD 25-35m loss, and a new TLBB IP mobile title is guided for late 2026/early 2027 (Q4 2025 call).

Borrow is easy and uncrowded (short interest 3.15% of float, borrow score 90/100), so the mechanical risk is not a squeeze but exit liquidity at ADT of USD 1.28m, which caps how much of a USD 345m market cap can be shorted at all.
catalysts: Q3 2026 results and whether games revenue surprises against Citi's below-expectation guidance.

theses.name: 111, Inc.
theses.one_liner: 111's founders bid USD 4.52 per ADS, a 29.5% premium, for a business whose 2Q26 revenue fell 28.3% y/y and whose TTM free cash flow yield is minus 67.8%.
theses.thesis: This is not a pure fundamental short; it is a takeover-arb situation sitting on a collapsing P&L. On 2026-09-17 the co-founders proposed a non-binding go-private at USD 4.52 per ADS, a 29.5% premium that lifted the stock 7.3% pre-market and drove ret_ytd to plus 40.2% even as the operating numbers deteriorate. The operating case is unambiguous: 2Q26 revenue fell 28.3% y/y with the loss widening, TTM revenue of RMB 11.29bn carries a minus 0.76% net margin, TTM free cash flow is minus RMB 88.9m (a minus 67.8% free-cash-flow yield on a USD 18.4m market cap), and revenue is falling at 33.2% y/y against a minus 4.08% three-year CAGR. The bet is therefore on the deal: if the founders walk and the board rejects, the fundamental picture reasserts and the equity has no operating floor; if the deal proceeds, the short is a fee-collecting arbitrage with capped upside.
bear_points: The core business is contracting hard: 2Q26 revenue fell 28.3% y/y with the loss widening, against TTM revenue decline of 33.2% y/y and a minus 4.08% three-year CAGR.

Cash is going out the door: TTM free cash flow is minus RMB 88.9m on RMB 11.29bn of revenue, a minus 67.8% free-cash-flow yield on the USD 18.4m market cap, and the screen flags both a 'cash burner' and a 'revenue collapse'.

The growth that exists is not the core: 2Q26 promotional products grew 121% to RMB 60.7m against net revenue of RMB 2,300.1m and an attributable loss of RMB 39.1m, so roughly 2.6% of revenue is growing while the other 97% shrinks.

The buyout premium is thin and revocable - 29.5%, or USD 0.226 per share above the undisturbed price - and the proposal is explicitly preliminary and non-binding with the board not yet having evaluated it, so the premium can disappear and re-rate the stock back toward its operating value.
Liquidity makes the outcome path-dependent: average daily turnover of about USD 54.8k is too thin to build or exit a short cleanly, and short interest is 1.0% of shares with 9,613 shares short.
risks_to_short: The dominant risk is that the deal closes: a USD 4.52 per ADS cash offer from the co-founders at a 29.5% premium drives the shares toward the offer and the short loses the spread plus borrow.
The balance sheet is net cash: a USD 18.4m market cap against an enterprise value of minus USD 27.79m implies roughly USD 28m of net cash, so a short here is short a cash box with no runway problem.
The insider signal is bullish, not bearish: the bid is founder-led with rollover and sponsor cash and is being read as a control buyout rather than distress.

The mechanics are as hostile as the fundamentals: borrow is not scarce (borrow component 50.0, short interest 1.0% of shares), there is no crowded short to harvest, and at roughly USD 54.8k of average daily turnover the float cannot absorb size - and the premium is already partly paid away, with the stock up 7.3% pre-market on the proposal and ret_ytd at plus 40.2%.
catalysts: Formalisation or withdrawal of the 2026-09-17 non-binding USD 4.52 per ADS go-private proposal, including the 6-K flagged as coming.

theses.name: Waterdrop, Inc. Class A
theses.one_liner: Waterdrop is buying 72.8% revenue growth with profit - GAAP net income fell 10.3% y/y in 2Q26 and 9.1% in 1Q26 - and quarterly net margin has fallen five straight quarters.

bear_points: Quarterly net margin has fallen five consecutive quarters, from 16.73% in 2Q25 to 7.92% in 1Q26, and 2Q26 GAAP net income was down 10.3% y/y to RMB 126m on 72.8% revenue growth (国元国际 2026-09-09).

Revenue growth of 72.8% y/y with insurance revenue up 80.5% and AI-attributed incremental premium of nearly RMB 100m is exactly the combination that re-rates a 4.9x P/E name upward on any two-quarter margin stabilisation.

Free cash flow of RMB 193.6m is 42.1% of revenue, a 90.3% FCF yield on the USD 30.2m market cap, in the same year the operating loss widened 5.6x - the cash flow statement and the income statement point in opposite directions.

If even part of the RMB 193.6m of FY2025 free cash flow is real and recurring, a distribution or capital-return announcement re-rates this rather than breaking it - the same cash flow that looks unreconciled is the bull case at a 90.3% FCF yield.

theses.name: Four Seasons Education (Cayman) Inc
theses.one_liner: Four Seasons Education turned FY2026 free cash flow positive only by cutting capex 89%: revenue fell 3.5%, gross margin is 26.8% against 41.0% three years earlier, and it trades USD 19k a day.
theses.thesis: The screen reads FY2026 as an inflection - a 12.1% net margin, a 13.8% FCF yield, net cash at 28.1% of a USD 23.1m market cap - but the cash came off the capex line: capex fell from RMB 57.3m in FY2025 to RMB 6.3m in FY2026 (-89.1%) while operating cash flow rose only RMB 8.7m, so RMB 51.0m of the RMB 59.7m swing to +RMB 22.6m of free cash flow is simply not spending. Underneath, growth stopped and the mix worsened: FY2026 revenue fell 3.5% to RMB 244.6m after +100.8% in FY2025, gross margin has fallen from 41.0% (FY2023) to 26.8% (FY2026) on roughly seven times the revenue, and the operating margin is 2.75%. With no company-specific broker note since January 2018, a USD 19.1k average daily tape and X carrying only WhatsApp promo, nobody is positioned to sell the re-rating case even if the margin recovery is real - which makes this a cheap-and-uncovered name rather than a mechanically forced one.
bear_points: The FY2026 free-cash-flow turn is a capex artifact: capex fell 89.1% to RMB 6.3m from RMB 57.3m while operating cash flow rose only RMB 8.7m to RMB 28.9m, so RMB 51.0m of the RMB 59.7m swing to +RMB 22.6m is the absence of investment rather than operating improvement.

Gross margin has compressed 14.2 points, from 41.0% in FY2023 to 26.8% in FY2026, even as revenue grew about seven-fold from RMB 34.9m to RMB 244.6m; the scale-up came at a structurally worse mix and leaves only a 2.75% operating margin.

Growth has rolled over: FY2026 revenue fell 3.5% y/y to RMB 244.6m after +100.8% in FY2025, so the screen's +91.4% three-year revenue CAGR is a base effect that is now exhausted, and the 2025-12-02 earnings-call transcript reporting H1 FY2026 revenue up 7.9% y/y is the last positive revenue datapoint in the bundle.

Three consecutive years of negative free cash flow preceded FY2026 (-RMB 34.7m in FY2023, -RMB 39.9m in FY2024, -RMB 37.1m in FY2025) while share count still grew 9.3% y/y, and the stock is down 32.2% over one year and 16.3% YTD.
